name: Plate-Loaded Lateral Raise (PL-LR)
source: Four ordered front-plane frames (perpendicular to the arm abduction plane) from the official Hammer Strength Plate-Loaded Lateral Raise demonstration (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4t2faIKsmr8, 0:09.1–0:09.9). Independent arm loaded with one 10 lb (4.54 kg) plate.

observation.evidence: Official Life Fitness / Hammer Strength front-plane demonstration (YouTube 4t2faIKsmr8, 0:09.1–0:09.9) of the Plate-Loaded Lateral Raise (PL-LR), cross-checked with the side view in the same video (0:03.5 and 0:15.0–0:18.0) showing each arm is a single rigid lever rotating in the frontal plane about an upper front-to-back bearing behind the shoulder (directly beneath the angled grey counterweight block), with the weight horn and forearm/elbow pad rigidly welded to the lower end of that same arm. The viewer's right workarm (lifter's left arm) is tracked across four ordered poses from bottom (~20 deg abduction) to top (~85 deg abduction) with one 10 lb Hammer Strength round urethane Olympic plate (4.54 kg) loaded on the arm. Slight forward camera dolly (~5% zoom across the 0.8 s clip) is tracked per pose and cancels in the lever force ratios. Rigid-lever invariants hold tightly across all four poses (radius ratio spread ~1.5%, angular offset spread <6 deg). Anatomical landmarks mark the left glenohumeral joint center, vertical trunk axis (proximal straight above joint so 0 deg = arm at side), and distal elbow pad contact; scale uses the visible Hammer Strength 10 lb round urethane plate outer diameter (10.04 in = 0.255 m per Life Fitness spec). Because the plate sits ~0.35 m behind the arm plane (~10% perspective foreshortening at ~3.5 m camera distance), the estimated joint moment arm carries ~10% systematic uncertainty (~0.25–0.31 m plausible range). Pivot verified by 50/50 motion overlay and concentric-circle fit at the rear shoulder-level bearing housing (near [590, 398]), reducing plate-radius spread from 26% to 2.1% and grip-radius spread from 24% to 7.7%.

base_resistance.source: Hammer Strength lists 1 lb (0.5 kg) starting resistance per workarm for the PL-LR. Unloaded curve across the stroke is unmeasured and held constant by default.
